transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… yeah, hi. I guess what really made me come in is work stuff. I’m a buyer, so I’m dealing with purchases and launch numbers and vendors all the time, and it’s like— I can’t shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking what I buy and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid.

My supervisor keeps showing me reports and saying they don’t prove that, but… I don’t know. Reports can be made to look clean, you know? Like when a display is set up wrong and everyone says it’s “just a mistake,” but then it happens three times. It’s been getting to me, and I figured I should talk to someone before it turns into a bigger thing.
Do you believe for certain that people at work are deliberately tracking what you buy and changing the numbers to make you look bad?

I mean… certain is a big word. But it feels pretty certain when it keeps lining up that way. Like, I’ll put buys in, and then the launch numbers look off, or a vendor suddenly acts like they know what I’m choosing before I even say it.

My supervisor keeps showing me the reports, like, “See, there’s no proof,” but reports are just numbers on a page. I used to help organize inventory sheets in high school for this fundraiser thing, and even then people could make stuff look normal if they wanted to. So… yeah, I can’t really shake it. It feels like they’re tracking what I buy and messing with things so I look bad.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

Yeah… sometimes. Not like all day or anything, but it happens.

Like if I’m in the stockroom, or sometimes driving back from a vendor meeting, I’ll hear this man’s voice like it’s right behind me. It’ll say stuff like, “Move faster, Scott,” or it’ll kind of laugh at the things I picked. And I’ll turn around, or look in the mirror if I’m driving, and there’s nobody there.

It’s weird because the stockroom has all these sounds anyway— carts, boxes, the lights buzzing— so at first I try to tell myself it’s just that. But sometimes it’s too clear.
Have you used any drugs recently, like cannabis, meth, cocaine, LSD, or anything similar?

Um… no, not really. I mean, I don’t think so. I’m not into meth or coke or anything like that.

Cannabis… people talk about it a lot, like at work or after work, but I’ve mostly stayed away from that stuff. My cousin used to make this whole big deal about how it “opens your mind,” and then he’d forget where he parked his car for like an hour, so… I don’t know, that never really appealed to me.

I’ve had drinks here and there, but for drugs like you listed, no, I haven’t used those recently.
Have you had any recent head injury, seizure, or other medical illness around the time these experiences started?

I don’t think so… not that I can connect to it, anyway. Like, there wasn’t some big thing where I got hurt and then everything started right after.

I mean, I’m trying to think, because sometimes weeks blur together when work gets busy, especially around shipments and vendor stuff. You’re running around, checking numbers, people asking for things, and then suddenly it’s Friday and you don’t even know what happened to Tuesday. But no, I don’t remember a seizure or some major illness or anything like that around when it started.

Unless you mean something smaller? I’m not sure what would count.
How long have these experiences been going on?

Um… I think it’s been, like, around ten months? Maybe a little under or over, but that’s the number that keeps coming to mind.

It’s hard to pin down because at first I wasn’t really keeping track, you know? I just thought I was stressed or tired from work, and then you get into the routine of shipments and checking prices and calling vendors, and everything sort of blends together. But the suspicious stuff and the voice… yeah, that’s been going on for about ten months now.
Have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have. Like on my days off, I mostly just sit in my apartment and scroll through sneaker drops, but I don’t even really care if I get anything. I’ll just keep looking anyway.

And my friends will text about volleyball or some gallery night—one of them got really into these little pop-up shows downtown, which used to be kind of fun, even if half the paintings look like someone spilled coffee on a receipt—but lately I just don’t answer. It feels like too much work to text back, even just to say I’m not coming.
During these past ten months, have you had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually high, energized, or needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I do get these stretches where it feels like the whole city is kind of opening up for me, like everything is moving and I can see all the angles. Like walking down a block and every store sign or delivery truck feels like it’s part of this big opportunity, if that makes sense.

And at work, during those times, I’ll be really keyed up about orders or buying stuff, like I know exactly what needs to happen. But then if somebody questions a purchase order, or tells me I should slow down, I just… snap. Way harder than I mean to. Like they’ll say one normal thing and I’ll feel this heat come up, like, why are you blocking this when I’m finally seeing it clearly?

So, yeah, I guess there have been periods like that. I don’t always think of it as “high,” exactly, but energized and kind of… untouchable, then irritated really fast.
Have there been at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling tracked even though you were not feeling especially energized or unusually down?

Yeah… yeah, I think so. There was this calmer stretch, like I wasn’t up all night or feeling like I had the whole market figured out or anything. I was sleeping more normal, going to work, doing the regular buyer stuff—checking inventory, prices, all that.

But even then, for a few weeks, I still thought people were tracking what I was buying. Like my orders meant something to someone. And I still heard the voice in the stockroom sometimes.

It’s weird because the stockroom has that buzzing light, and there’s this one shelf that always leans no matter how many times we fix it—sorry, that’s not the point. The point is, yeah, it wasn’t only when I was all energized or really down. It kept happening even when I was more… level, I guess.
During these past ten months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d say two weeks like that. I mean, I’ve had bad days, yeah, where I don’t want to get out of bed or I just kind of move around slow, but I don’t really track it on a calendar.

Like, sometimes the whole week feels gray, and then I’ll realize I still went to work and bought groceries, or I spent an hour looking at some jacket online I wasn’t even going to buy. So… I’m not sure. Two weeks straight, most of the day every day? I can’t really say for sure.
During those energized periods, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yeah… during those stretches, sleep feels kind of optional. Like I’ll sleep maybe three or four hours, and then I wake up already wired, like my body’s saying, get up, there’s stuff to do.

And lying there feels stupid, honestly, like wasted time. I’ll start thinking about orders or deals or whatever moves I should be making, and then I’m just up. It’s not like normal tired where you’re dragging the next day. I feel ready. Like more ready than usual.
When the voice first started, were you feeling unusually energized at that time?

Yeah… I think when it first really started, I was in one of those wired stretches. I wasn’t sleeping much at all, and I kept talking about sneaker trends, like I had figured out what everyone was about to buy before they knew it.

At work I felt kind of untouchable, like I could move faster than everybody else. And around then I was also thinking the vendors were messing with the numbers, like manipulating them somehow. The voice was there too sometimes, like pushing me to go quicker, make the move faster.

I mean, it’s hard to separate because work already has so many numbers and vendor stuff, and people do play games with pricing—sorry, yeah, the answer is yes, I was unusually energized then.
During one of those energized periods, were you ever hospitalized because of it?

I don’t think so. I mean, nobody took me to a hospital for being energized, if that’s what you mean.

There were times people were like, “You need to calm down,” or they’d look at me like I was doing too much, but hospital? No… not that I remember. I’ve been around hospitals for other stuff, like visiting people, and the waiting rooms always have that weird vending machine smell, but for one of those periods specifically, no, I don’t think that happened.
Have any of those unusually energized, needing-little-sleep periods lasted at least a week?

Yeah, I mean… it’s hard to count it cleanly because it kind of comes and goes, and then I’ll get distracted trying to remember what week was what. But those high-energy, barely-sleeping stretches have been going on in my life for, like, around eleven months now.

Like, not every single day is the same, but it’s been part of things for almost a year.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

I’m not really sure. Like, I’ve had down days, yeah, where everything feels heavy, but two weeks nearly every day… I don’t know how to count that exactly.

Sometimes the days blur together, especially if work is weird or I’m just not keeping track. I remember once I thought I’d been sad for a whole month, but then I realized part of that was just being stuck inside because the weather was bad and my phone screen had cracked, and I kept putting off fixing it. So… I don’t know. I can’t say for sure it was two weeks nearly every day.
For at least one month, were you hearing the voice or feeling tracked while not feeling unusually energized or depressed?

Yeah… I think so. There was a calmer stretch, like I wasn’t all revved up and I was sleeping more normal, not feeling like I was running the whole market or anything.

But even then, for a few weeks I still had this thing where I felt like people were tracking my buys. And I’d hear the voice in the stockroom sometimes. The stockroom has this buzzing light too, which makes it worse, and there’s always boxes stacked weird, like nobody ever puts the canned stuff where it’s supposed to go… but yeah, that was happening even when my mood was more level, I guess.
During those energized stretches, did you take on a lot more activities or projects than usual?

Yeah, definitely. When I’m keyed up I can’t just do one thing. I’ll be emailing three different vendors, then making a buy plan, then suddenly reorganizing samples because they “need” to be in the right order, and then I’m pacing around the office like if I sit down I’ll lose the whole thread.

It’s like everything feels connected and urgent. Even stuff that probably could wait, I’ll start it all at once.
For six months or more, have you been hearing the voice or feeling that people were tracking you?

Yeah… it’s been longer than six months. I mean, I didn’t mark it on a calendar or anything, but the voice and the feeling like people are watching or tracking what I’m doing with buys… that’s been going on maybe around ten months.

It kind of started feeling like it was just part of the background after a while, like the way the store has that same hum all day and you stop noticing until someone points it out. But yeah, roughly ten months, I think.
Have you ever had a time lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

I don’t know… depressed like every day for two weeks, I’m not sure. I get down sometimes, like anyone does, and some days I’m just kind of flat, but I don’t really keep track of it like that.

Two weeks is a weird amount of time to measure, because at work the weeks blur together, especially when shipments come in late and everyone’s asking where the order is, and then I’m thinking about that instead of how I feel. So… I guess I can’t say for sure.
Over these past ten or eleven months, have those energized, needing-less-sleep periods taken up most of the time overall?

Yeah… looking back, I think so. Most of the time it’s been more like I’m wired, or I’m irritated because people are moving too slow, and I’m taking on too much at work because it feels like I can handle all of it.

There are calmer stretches, but they don’t feel like the main thing. It’s more like I get a little break, and then I’m back to overworking, talking myself into these big plans, feeling really sure I’m right, and people have to kind of… slow me down, or try to. Like with buying stuff, if you don’t move fast you miss the deal, and then everyone blames you for not having the right stock—sorry, that’s not exactly what you asked. But yeah, overall, most of these past months have been those keyed-up stretches, with shorter normal periods in between.

doctor.question: During those energized periods, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep
target_item.manifestation: There have been plenty of weeks where I sleep maybe three or four hours, wake up feeling wired and ready, and think lying in bed is just wasting time I could use to make moves.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether, during energized periods, I needed much less sleep than usual and still felt rested, which directly matches decreased need for sleep.

patient.answer:
Yeah… during those stretches, sleep feels kind of optional. Like I’ll sleep maybe three or four hours, and then I wake up already wired, like my body’s saying, get up, there’s stuff to do.

And lying there feels stupid, honestly, like wasted time. I’ll start thinking about orders or deals or whatever moves I should be making, and then I’m just up. It’s not like normal tired where you’re dragging the next day. I feel ready. Like more ready than usual.

inference.note: Reduced likelihood of F23 and F06.2: symptoms have persisted ~10 months, arguing against acute/transient psychosis, and there is no clear substance/medical/neurologic trigger. Presence of psychosis for at least 2 weeks outside mood episodes supports F25.0 over F31.2, though bipolar I with psychotic features remains possible because clear decreased need for sleep and energized periods are present. F20.0 remains in the differential given chronic delusions, hallucinations, and negative symptoms.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have ever occurred exclusively during mood episodes or also clearly outside them, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: When the voice first started, were you feeling unusually energized at that time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: During the weeks when I was barely sleeping, talking nonstop about sneaker trends, and feeling untouchable at work, I was also convinced vendors were manipulating the numbers and sometimes heard that voice pushing me to move faster.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the hallucinated voice began during an unusually energized period, which is about whether psychotic symptoms occurred at the same time as manic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think when it first really started, I was in one of those wired stretches. I wasn’t sleeping much at all, and I kept talking about sneaker trends, like I had figured out what everyone was about to buy before they knew it.

At work I felt kind of untouchable, like I could move faster than everybody else. And around then I was also thinking the vendors were messing with the numbers, like manipulating them somehow. The voice was there too sometimes, like pushing me to go quicker, make the move faster.

I mean, it’s hard to separate because work already has so many numbers and vendor stuff, and people do play games with pricing—sorry, yeah, the answer is yes, I was unusually energized then.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a full manic episode severe enough to cause marked impairment or hospitalization, which would help distinguish bipolar I disorder with psychotic features from schizoaffective disorder and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: During one of those energized periods, were you ever hospitalized because of it?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically whether an energized/manic period led to hospitalization, but the provided symptom profile does not include any hospitalization history or treatment setting information.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so. I mean, nobody took me to a hospital for being energized, if that’s what you mean.

There were times people were like, “You need to calm down,” or they’d look at me like I was doing too much, but hospital? No… not that I remember. I’ve been around hospitals for other stuff, like visiting people, and the waiting rooms always have that weird vending machine smell, but for one of those periods specifically, no, I don’t think that happened.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had a full manic episode lasting at least one week, which helps distinguish bipolar I disorder with psychotic features from schizoaffective disorder and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have any of those unusually energized, needing-little-sleep periods lasted at least a week?

target_item.name: Manic Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The elevated, irritable, high-energy stretches have been part of my life for about eleven months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the unusually energized, decreased-sleep periods, specifically whether they lasted at least a week.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean… it’s hard to count it cleanly because it kind of comes and goes, and then I’ll get distracted trying to remember what week was what. But those high-energy, barely-sleeping stretches have been going on in my life for, like, around eleven months now.

Like, not every single day is the same, but it’s been part of things for almost a year.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had a major depressive episode, which would help distinguish schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a depressive episode lasting at least two weeks, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depressive mood symptom or major depressive episode item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. Like, I’ve had down days, yeah, where everything feels heavy, but two weeks nearly every day… I don’t know how to count that exactly.

Sometimes the days blur together, especially if work is weird or I’m just not keeping track. I remember once I thought I’d been sad for a whole month, but then I realized part of that was just being stuck inside because the weather was bad and my phone screen had cracked, and I kept putting off fixing it. So… I don’t know. I can’t say for sure it was two weeks nearly every day.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least one month in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and support schizophrenia-spectrum diagnosis.
doctor.question: For at least one month, were you hearing the voice or feeling tracked while not feeling unusually energized or depressed?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys and hearing the voice in the stockroom.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the psychotic symptoms—hearing the voice or feeling tracked—occurred for a sustained period while not unusually energized or depressed, which directly matches this requirement.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. There was a calmer stretch, like I wasn’t all revved up and I was sleeping more normal, not feeling like I was running the whole market or anything.

But even then, for a few weeks I still had this thing where I felt like people were tracking my buys. And I’d hear the voice in the stockroom sometimes. The stockroom has this buzzing light too, which makes it worse, and there’s always boxes stacked weird, like nobody ever puts the canned stuff where it’s supposed to go… but yeah, that was happening even when my mood was more level, I guess.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the elevated periods included abnormally increased goal-directed activity, which would strengthen mania over schizophrenia-spectrum illness now that psychosis outside mood episodes suggests schizoaffective disorder vs bipolar I with psychotic features.
doctor.question: During those energized stretches, did you take on a lot more activities or projects than usual?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity
target_item.manifestation: When I'm keyed up I can't just handle one task, so I'll be emailing three vendors, making a buy plan, reorganizing samples, and pacing the office like stopping would make me lose the thread.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether, during energized stretches, I took on more activities or projects than usual, which directly matches increased goal-directed activity or energy.

patient.answer:
Yeah, definitely. When I’m keyed up I can’t just do one thing. I’ll be emailing three different vendors, then making a buy plan, then suddenly reorganizing samples because they “need” to be in the right order, and then I’m pacing around the office like if I sit down I’ll lose the whole thread.

It’s like everything feels connected and urgent. Even stuff that probably could wait, I’ll start it all at once.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have persisted for at least six months overall, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder and bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: For six months or more, have you been hearing the voice or feeling that people were tracking you?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the voice and tracking beliefs have been occurring, specifically whether they lasted six months or more.

patient.answer:
Yeah… it’s been longer than six months. I mean, I didn’t mark it on a calendar or anything, but the voice and the feeling like people are watching or tracking what I’m doing with buys… that’s been going on maybe around ten months.

It kind of started feeling like it was just part of the background after a while, like the way the store has that same hum all day and you stop noticing until someone points it out. But yeah, roughly ten months, I think.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has ever had a major depressive episode, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder bipolar type from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about a depressive episode lasting at least two weeks, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depression-related item.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… depressed like every day for two weeks, I’m not sure. I get down sometimes, like anyone does, and some days I’m just kind of flat, but I don’t really keep track of it like that.

Two weeks is a weird amount of time to measure, because at work the weeks blur together, especially when shipments come in late and everyone’s asking where the order is, and then I’m thinking about that instead of how I feel. So… I guess I can’t say for sure.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the manic symptoms occupied the majority of the total illness duration, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features now that psychosis has also occurred outside mood episodes.
doctor.question: Over these past ten or eleven months, have those energized, needing-less-sleep periods taken up most of the time overall?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, most of the time since this all started has been taken up by those wired or irritable stretches where I was overworking, overconfident, and hard to slow down, with only shorter calmer periods in between.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the energized, decreased-sleep/manic periods occupied most of the overall illness duration, which directly matches this requirement.

patient.answer:
Yeah… looking back, I think so. Most of the time it’s been more like I’m wired, or I’m irritated because people are moving too slow, and I’m taking on too much at work because it feels like I can handle all of it.

There are calmer stretches, but they don’t feel like the main thing. It’s more like I get a little break, and then I’m back to overworking, talking myself into these big plans, feeling really sure I’m right, and people have to kind of… slow me down, or try to. Like with buying stuff, if you don’t move fast you miss the deal, and then everyone blames you for not having the right stock—sorry, that’s not exactly what you asked. But yeah, overall, most of these past months have been those keyed-up stretches, with shorter normal periods in between.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) for about 10 months, with at least a 1-month period of psychosis when mood was relatively level, ruling against a purely mood-congruent bipolar psychosis. He also has clear manic symptoms lasting at least a week and occupying most of the illness duration overall, supporting schizoaffective disorder, manic type, over bipolar I disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia.
